title: Taiwan Isn’t Giving Up, It’s Pulling Apart
author: Dennis Lu-Chung Weng
text:
A KMT-led rally on July 20, 2025, urges a “no” vote in the July 26 recalls.
Credit: Wikimedia Commons/ Tieguanyin1990
In a recent article for The Diplomat, Mor Sobol offered an even-handed assessment of the debate set off by Simon Shuster’s piece in The Atlantic, which asked whether Taiwan might simply “give up” under growing pressure from China. Sobol argued that both Shuster’s pessimistic answer and his critics’ confident rebuttals rest on thinner evidence than either side recognizes. Sobol pointed out that telling a pollster “I would defend Taiwan” is very different from making that decision when missiles are falling, and that Taiwan is not a unitary actor. The question worth asking is how the trends in public opinion, military recruitment, defense spending and other metrics move over time, not what any single snapshot shows.[...]
